title: Architecture & Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance, and ADRs
author: Maya Patel
body:
Overview

Purpose: This document consolidates Redwood Inference's engineering architecture and standards for API design, code quality, infrastructure, model-serving, observability, and performance. It is intended as the canonical reference for engineers responsible for building and operating inference services, SDKs, and platform components.

Scope: Applies to all services and components within Redwood Inference (hosted API, Dedicated, Private control plane, and runtime components). Exceptions must be approved via an ADR and recorded in the ADRs section below.

Principles
- Developer-first: APIs and tools should optimize for fast developer iteration and clear error semantics.
- Production-safe by default: Authentication, rate limits, retries, and circuit breakers are configured conservatively out of the box.
- Observable and debuggable: Every service must emit structured logs, metrics, and traces for critical paths.
- Backwards compatible: Public APIs must follow versioning rules to preserve customer integrations.
- Measurable performance: Define SLOs and automated alerting for latency/availability and cost per token.

1) API Standards\n(Owner: API Platform / eng-developer-experience)

1.1 Design and format
- API style: REST for simple resources (customers, routes), gRPC or HTTP/2+JSON for low-latency streaming endpoints (generation, streaming chat).
- Versioning: Use semantic versioned paths for breaking changes: /v1/, /v2/. Avoid roll-your-own headers for major versioning.
- Path & naming conventions: kebab-case for resource names, use nouns for resources and sub-resources (e.g., /projects/{id}/routes).

1.2 Authentication & Authorization
- Primary auth: bearer tokens (short-lived with rotation for internal services). All customer-facing endpoints require TLS and token auth.
- RBAC: Enforce least privilege via role claims in tokens for control-plane operations.

1.3 Error handling
- Use consistent HTTP status codes. Body must include {"error": {"code": string, "message": string, "meta": {}}}.
- Standard error codes: INVALID_INPUT, UNAUTHORIZED, FORBIDDEN, RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, BACKEND_ERROR, MODEL_UNAVAILABLE.

1.4 Pagination & Filtering
- Cursor-based pagination for large lists. Response: { items: [], next_cursor: string | null }.
- Filtering: allow indexed fields only; request-level limits enforced (max_page_size = 1000).

1.5 Rate limiting & quotas
- Tenant-level default: 100 requests/min for free-tier, configurable for paid customers. Enforcement at the API gateway with burst capacity rules.

1.6 Compatibility & Deprecation
- Deprecation policy: 90 days notice for non-breaking behavior changes, 180 days for breaking changes. Document deprecation in release notes and send tenant notifications.

API Example (generation request):
POST /v1/generate
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>, Content-Type: application/json
Body:
{
  "model": "redwood-1-alpha",
  "prompt": "Summarize the following...",
  "max_tokens": 256,
  "temperature": 0.0
}

2) Coding Standards
(Owner: Engineering Leads)

2.1 Languages & Repositories
- Primary service languages: Go for control-plane and networking-critical components; Rust for performance-critical runtime kernels; Python for evaluation and orchestration scripts; TypeScript for frontend/console.
- Mono-repo policy: infra and core platform libraries live in monorepos with service-level submodules where necessary.

2.2 Style & Linting
- Adopt company-wide linters and formatter configs: gofmt/go vet, rustfmt/clippy, black/isort/flake8 for Python, ESLint/Prettier for TypeScript. PRs must be green on linters and unit tests.

2.3 Testing & CI
- Minimum test coverage: services must include unit tests; critical path code must include integration tests.
- CI gates: format, lint, unit tests, security scan, dependency audit. Deployable artifact only if pipeline passes.

2.4 Code Review & Ownership
- Minimum 2 approvers for production changes: one service owner and one cross-team reviewer.
- Use CODEOWNERS file to enforce reviewers by path.

2.5 Secrets & Credentials
- Do not store secrets in repo. Use Vault/KMS integrations and short-lived credentials.

3) Infrastructure Standards
(Owner: eng-infra)

3.1 IaC and Environment Parity
- Primary IaC: Terraform for provisioning cloud resources; Helm + Kustomize for Kubernetes manifests.
- Environment tiers: dev, staging, preprod, prod. Parity required between staging and prod for networking and IAM.

3.2 Networking & Regions
- VPC naming: vpc-{env}-{region}-{team}. Subnets: public/private with clear NAT/gateway boundaries.
- Cross-region failover: critical services in at least 2 regions (NA, EU) with automated DNS failover and health checks.

3.3 Capacity & GPU Fleet
- GPU instance types: use ML-optimized instances (A100/H100) for Dedicated pools. Default images should be hardened and include kernel versions tested by runtime team.
- Autoscaling: scale based on queue depth and p95 serving latency. Minimum pool sizes defined per service.

3.4 Secrets & Key Management
- Customer keys: stored in customer-managed KMS where required for Private deployments; otherwise use Redwood-managed KMS with strict access controls.

3.5 Backups & Disaster Recovery
- Critical state (customer configs, billing records) backed up daily with 30-day retention; test restores quarterly.

4) Model-serving Standards
(Owner: eng-serving-runtime / applied-ml-and-evals)

4.1 Model Versioning & Artifacts
- Model artifacts: immutable storage with content-addressable IDs. Every model has metadata: model_id, architecture, tokenizer_spec, quantization_profile, provenance (source + commit), and compatibility matrix.
- Versioning: semantic for API-facing model names (e.g., redwood-1-alpha@v1.2.0).

4.2 Container images & runtime configs
- Image naming: registry.redwood.io/model-host:{model_id}-{sha}. Images must be scanned for vulnerabilities and signed.
- Runtime knobs: kv_cache_size, max_concurrent_requests, batch_window_ms. Default profiles provided by quantization-profiles directory.

4.3 Input/output validation
- Strict schema validation on all inbound requests; reject malformed requests with INVALID_INPUT. Outputs must conform to declared response schema.

4.4 Fallbacks & Graceful Degradation
- Multi-variant routing: route first to primary model variant, fallback to smaller/quantized variant on capacity or degraded metrics. Circuit-breakers to fail fast with informative error codes.

4.5 Quantization & Precision
- Quantization profiles should be registered alongside the model and must include validated quality regression metrics (per prompt set). Only approved quantization profiles are used in production rollout.

4.6 Rollouts & Canary
- Canary policy: 1% initial traffic, monitor latency, error rate, and quality regressions for 24 hours before progressive rollout (1%, 5%, 25%, 100%). Automatic rollback on predefined regression thresholds (see Performance & Quality gates).

5) Observability Standards
(Owner: eng-platform / eng-sre)

5.1 Metrics
- Emit high-cardinality tags sparingly. Standard metrics for serving: request_count, request_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99 histograms), tokens_generated, kv_cache_hit_ratio, batch_size.
- Metric names: namespace.service.metric (e.g., inference.model-host.request_latency_ms).

5.2 Tracing
- Use open telemetry (OTel) with 200ms sampling for regular traffic; 100% sampling for error traces. Include trace context through async boundaries.

5.3 Logging
- Structured JSON logs with fields: timestamp, level, service, trace_id, span_id, request_id, tenant_id, message, error_code, latency_ms. Logs should avoid PII and model inputs unless explicitly enabled and audited.

5.4 Dashboards & Alerts
- Default dashboards: per-model latency heatmap, cluster utilization, GPU memory pressure, eviction rates, and tenant error rates.
- Alerting thresholds: p95 latency > service_target * 1.5 for 5m, error_rate > 5% for 5m, kv_cache_hit_ratio < 0.3 for 10m. Critical pager for prod SLO breaches.

6) Performance Standards & SLOs
(Owner: eng-sre / eng-serving-runtime)

6.1 Latency SLOs (example targets, adjust per model class)
- Hosted API (short sequences, <= 128 tokens): p50 <= 50ms, p95 <= 200ms, availability 99.9%.
- Dedicated inference (customer reserved capacity): p95 <= 150ms, throughput SLA as contracted.
- Embeddings endpoints: p95 <= 100ms for small vectors.

6.2 Throughput & Batching
- Batch sizing: default dynamic batching up to 32 requests; min viable batch window 8ms for low-latency tiers.
- Batching tradeoffs documented per model in quantization-profiles and model descriptors.

6.3 Cost & Efficiency
- Per-token cost target: track cost_per_1k_tokens by model variant and enforce budget alerts when > 2x baseline for > 24h.

6.4 Quality & Regression Gates
- Every model change (new weights, quantization) must pass automated eval against canonical prompt-sets (see applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks) with no worse than 1% degradation on critical metrics or require explicit sign-off.

7) Operational Runbook Summaries
- Incident triage: follow oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process. For serving degradations: (1) identify impact (tenants, models), (2) switch affected routes to fallback variants, (3) scale pools or rollback deployment, (4) notify customers and execs if SLA at risk.
- Common playbooks: model OOMs, KV cache thrashing, GPU host failure, and autoscaler runaway. Detailed runbooks live in eng-serving-runtime/runbooks.

8) Decision Records (ADRs) Summary
- ADR-2024-01: Standardize on Go for control plane services (Rationale: low-latency networking, strong ecosystem).
- ADR-2024-07: Adopt content-addressable model artifacts and semantic model versioning.
- ADR-2025-03: Use Terraform + Helm for infra provisioning and k8s manifests.
- ADR-2025-11: Default to OpenTelemetry for distributed tracing.
- ADR-2026-02: Introduced multi-variant fallback routing for model availability.

For each ADR include: title, status, decision date, summary, alternatives considered, and owner. Full ADR documents are stored under confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records and must be referenced by ADR ID in new proposals.

9) Governance & Exceptions
- Exceptions: Teams may request a documented exception by filing an ADR and obtaining approvals from architecture review board (members: eng leads, infra, SRE, security).
- Reviews: Architecture standards reviewed quarterly. Critical changes require phased rollout and cross-team signoffs.

Appendices
A. Config table (examples)
- service: inference-router
  - target_p95_ms: 200
  - default_batch_window_ms: 8
  - max_batch_size: 32
- service: model-host
  - kv_cache_size: 8GB
  - max_concurrent_requests: 64
  - fallback_variant: quantized-8bit

B. Release & Deprecation checklist
1. Create migration guide and changelog.
2. Run integration tests against staging and preprod.
3. Notify customers and schedule deprecation window.
4. Monitor metrics and listen for rollback signals.

C. Contacts & Ownership
